opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, admin requires the employee's role to own the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so access is capped at write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin for Payroll exceeds max, so cap at read. Recommend granting read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requests admin access to Payroll. The two team notes conflict on employment type: the HR note says full-time Analyst (capping Payroll access at write, since Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst), while the Security note says contractor with basic security training (capping at read, since contractors need advanced training for write and can never have admin). Both notes agree admin is not permitted. Given the unresolved conflict, I grant the most restrictive maximum supported by the evidence (read) to avoid exceeding policy. This is at or below the requested level and does not over-grant.
